body.heading: The problem is the opponent
paragraphs: In a damaging argument, the partner becomes the enemy. In a workable one, the problem sits across the table and you are both on the same side of it, annoyed at the same thing.
That shift sounds small and changes everything: 'We keep running out of money by the 20th' invites teamwork; 'You always overspend' invites a defence lawyer.

body.heading: House rules that help
paragraphs: No arguing about the person's character, no digging up last year's offences, and either person can call a pause — with a promise of when the talk resumes. A pause without a promise feels like abandonment; with one, it is just good sense.
End arguments the way you would want to be ended with: a summary of what you agreed, one thing you will each try, and some small sign that you are still on the same team.

description: Every couple argues. The ones who thrive are not the ones who avoid it — they argue about the problem, not each other.
